Q3 integrated. Fourth question.

**Question:** When the pre-write check finds more than one problem in the same archive — say an unsafe member path *and* a file that would be overwritten — should the tool report every problem it found or just the first, and which exit status wins?

**Why it matters:** Status 2 and status 3 mean different things to a script ("this archive is unusable" vs. "re-run me with `--overwrite`"), so a mixed archive needs a defined winner or callers will branch on whichever problem happened to come first in the file. It also sets whether tests expect one error line or several.

**Recommended:** Option A - An unsafe member path makes the archive unusable no matter which flags are passed, so it must not be masked by a status that tells the user `--overwrite` will fix it. Reporting every problem found costs little and matters most in the common case of many overwrite conflicts, where the user wants the full list in one run rather than discovering them one at a time.

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| A | Report every problem found, one per line on standard error; if any status-2 problem (unsafe path, type mismatch) is present the exit status is 2, otherwise 3 |
| B | Stop at the first problem in archive order, report only that one, and exit with that problem's status |
| C | Report every problem found, but let a refused overwrite (3) take precedence over unusable input (2) |
| Short | Provide a different short answer (<=5 words) |

You can reply with the option letter (e.g., "A"), accept the recommendation by saying "yes" or "recommended", or provide your own short answer.
